advisory.finding: No test exercises the pyproject.toml-named pointer branch: layer_llm_config_file reads [tool.rebar.llm] only when path.name=='pyproject.toml' (pyproject=(path.name=='pyproject.toml')), but every pointer file in the suite is named 'ci.toml' (default of _pointer). A regression that drops the pyproject argument — reading the top-level [llm] table instead of [tool.rebar.llm] for a pyproject-named pointer — would pass every existing test.
merged_from: The documented contract that the REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE pointer is layered OUTSIDE the malformed-core-config degrade (discovered={} on ConfigError, then still deep-merged) is untested. No test combines a malformed/unparseable discovered config with a valid pointer, so a regression moving layer_llm_config_file inside the try/except (letting a broken pyproject swallow the pointer) would go uncaught.

The blank/whitespace-only pointer no-op guard is untested: llm_config_file_pointer returns None when raw.strip() is falsy, distinguishing a blank REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE from an unset one and from a real path. No test sets a blank value, so a regression that treats blank as a path (raising ConfigError on Path('').is_file()) instead of a clean no-op would not be caught.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test using _pointer(..., name='pyproject.toml') with a '[tool.rebar]\n[tool.rebar.llm]\nmodel = ...' body, asserting the resolved model comes from that table.
